overview: The Council addressed safety concerns regarding new traffic infrastructure on High Street and received a status report on the Green Line Extension project. They also discussed emergency heat protocols for senior housing and approved temporary food truck permits.

items.title: High Street Traffic Island Concerns
items.summary: The Council passed an amended resolution expressing safety concerns regarding a newly installed traffic island at the intersection of High Street, Woburn Street, and Hastings Lane. Discussion focused on the narrow roadway width and potential hazards for emergency vehicles and large trucks.

items.title: Medford Chess Club Riverside Avenue Park Meetings
items.summary: Councilors approved a resolution supporting the Medford Chess Club's use of Riverside Avenue Park, including requests for permanent concrete tables and increased police patrols.

items.title: Green Line Extension Project Update
items.summary: Community representatives reported that the Green Line Extension project is facing delays due to pandemic-related supply chain issues, though 'South Medford' has been successfully included in the Ball Square station name.

items.title: Air Conditioning Failure at 99 Riverside Avenue
items.summary: The Council requested an explanation from management for failing to activate air conditioning during a recent heat wave and discussed the adequacy of city-run cooling stations and emergency management. The body also moved to investigate potential state law changes regarding mandatory heating dates that conflict with extreme temperatures.

items.title: Condolences for Francis 'Bud' Kelly
items.summary: The Council paid tribute to former athletic director and coach Francis Bud Kelly and dedicated the meeting to his memory.

items.title: Food Truck Permit Approvals
items.summary: Permits were approved for the Sausage Guy to operate at Hormel Stadium and for a temporary Dunkin' Donuts mobile cart to serve customers during building renovations.

items.title: Committee Reports and Routine Business
items.summary: The Council advanced a Water Board report for its first reading, acknowledged ongoing budget deliberations, and approved meeting records.
